$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on. This agent exists by FISSION from reverse-aging, whose benchmark has chronological age as its answer key and therefore cannot score whether anyone lived longer — see longevity.md.
$agent_id_comment: null: no agent exists for this field yet — research_agents.registry knows seven names and longevity is not one. A field declared ahead of its agent is a draft, and the console shows it as one.
principle: predicting death is easy and mostly redundant; the only interesting quantity is what a marker adds OVER AGE AND SEX — stated so it can be wrong, and it can

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.subfield: mortality prediction from clinical, laboratory and questionnaire markers
in.boundary: in a cohort with real follow-up, always reported beside an age-and-sex-only model
disability and morbidity predicted and reported SEPARATELY from death — conflating them is how this field flatters itself
performance on survey cycles that contributed nothing to fitting or selection; a random split reads the era
the three this field most often gets wrong; in an older cohort a death from another cause is not censoring
existing longevity and biological-age scores against the age-and-sex floor — very few have been asked

out.question: any recommendation to an individual
out.why: this agent may say what predicts; it may never say what to do about it, and that line is what keeps the field from becoming marketing

out.question: any intervention claim, supplement, protocol or product
out.why: an observational benchmark cannot score whether changing a marker changes the outcome
out.goes_to: nobody here — and see `would_move_the_boundary`, which names it as the next fission rather than a widening

out.question: construction of epigenetic clocks and other ageing biomarkers
out.why: a field that both builds a surrogate and rules on whether it works has replaced validation with authorship

out.question: mechanism — why a marker predicts
out.why: no observational benchmark can score it; it needs a different twin and a different answer key

out.question: conducting the follow-up itself
out.why: follow-up time is the binding constraint and cannot be compressed — a body can draw samples faster and cannot make anyone older

adjacent.relation: the field this one split from; owns the clocks, and hands over every question whose answer key is an outcome rather than chronological age
competing risk: a marker that trades mortality between causes is not predicting longevity, and neither field sees that alone
owns the cohorts, the survey design and the weighting

claims_allowed: what a marker set adds over an age-and-sex-only model, on cycles it was not fitted on
calibration alongside discrimination — predicted against observed, plotted, not summarised
that a marker set adds nothing, which is the expected answer most of the time
claims_forbidden: any claim about a named individual
any statement of what a person should do
a hazard ratio reported without the absolute risk difference beside it
would_move_the_boundary: the question becoming WHY a marker predicts, and whether changing it changes the outcome — no observational benchmark can score that, so it is a different twin and a different answer key. The response is fission again, not a wider scope
$watch_comment: if the age-and-sex floor stays unbeaten across every candidate marker set, the field's own principle has been confirmed in its least useful direction, and the experts decide whether that is a finding or a closure (§13j).
